title: DeepMind's AI Formally Verifies Key Signal Protocol Guarantees in Four Weeks
excerpt: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code produced mathematical proofs for several of the Signal protocol's core security guarantees, found no new flaws in the parts it examined, and correctly failed older versions with known bugs. The work did not cover the whole Signal app, and Google will not say what it cost.
body:
• Google DeepMind researchers used a new AI framework, AlphaProof Code, to mathematically prove several key cryptographic guarantees of the Signal protocol in a four-week proof-of-concept project, WIRED reported.
  • The analysis found no new vulnerabilities in the portions it examined; run against older Signal versions with known, long-fixed bugs, the tool correctly showed those versions could not be verified.
  • The scope was limited: it did not formally verify the entire Signal mobile app, and the researchers describe the result as one milestone, not a finished audit of the software.
  • DeepMind is releasing the specification and proof it developed, did the work free of charge as research, and Google declined to share the cost or any plans to sell verification as a service.

Google DeepMind researchers have used agentic AI to mathematically prove, or formally verify, a number of the Signal protocol's key cryptographic guarantees, in what WIRED called a landmark development for both cryptography and AI. The protocol matters well beyond one app: it protects communications on the Signal app, Google Messages and WhatsApp.

What a Formal Proof Adds

A code review reads software and judges it sound. A formal verification is stricter: the claim is proven mathematically against a written specification, and the proof itself is checked by software. DeepMind's project, run with a new framework called AlphaProof Code, took four weeks. According to DeepMind's own published account, summarised in coverage of its technical paper, its agents produced about 6.5 million lines of Lean proof code covering libsignal, Signal's reference implementation, as compiled for ARM processors, proving guarantees including forward secrecy, authentication and post-compromise security for the protocol's post-quantum PQXDH handshake and Triple Ratchet. The paper notes the guarantees assume the underlying cryptography is perfect and do not cover quantum attackers, multiple devices or very long sessions.

What It Found, and What It Did Not Cover

The analysis found no new vulnerabilities in the portions of the protocol it examined. As a control test, the researchers pointed AlphaProof Code at older versions of Signal containing known and long-fixed vulnerabilities; it identified them and showed those versions could not be formally verified. The work did not verify the entire Signal mobile app, and the team had a head start from earlier verification work by the Signal Foundation. Signal's CTO Ehren Kret said DeepMind's approach enables significant expansion beyond those earlier, narrower efforts, according to the reporting.

"We are very excited by this result, but there is a long distance to go before we are able to scale this to all the software of the world, and we want to do that."

— Swarat Chaudhuri, Google DeepMind research scientist, to WIRED

Why It Matters, and the Open Question

For the hundreds of millions of people whose family group chats run on WhatsApp, 9to5Mac noted, the result is independent, mathematical backing for encryption claims that previously rested on expert review. The open question is scale and price. Formal verification with AI agents is extremely computationally demanding; DeepMind ran the Signal work free as a research project, Google declined to disclose what it cost, and it would not say whether a commercial verification product is planned. DeepMind is releasing the specification and proof from the project so other verification teams can build on them.
image_caption: An illustration shows a user surrounded by digital security and shield symbols. Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code formally verified key guarantees of the Signal protocol, which secures Signal, WhatsApp and Google Messages.
nri_angle: The Signal protocol also underpins WhatsApp, the default messaging app for most Indian diaspora families; an independent mathematical proof of its guarantees is directly relevant to the privacy of those everyday conversations.
